body_json.answer:
**Assessment:** rejected.

The new post's general skepticism toward "official accounts and media coverage" echoes the media-distrust framing in T4-009510, which argues that because the New York Times "can't even verify a Twitter account," readers shouldn't "accept their other reporting" [T4-009510](#T4-009510), and in T4-008246, which mocks outlets reporting on fake news as "Fake News" [T4-008246](#T4-008246). T4-008934 similarly faults a reporter for "tip-toeing around the Truth" and suggests a career change [T4-008934](#T4-008934). A meaningful difference is that the new post is an abstract, category-level claim with no named outlet or incident, whereas the retrieved posts attack specific outlets or journalists over particular alleged failures. T4-005389 runs somewhat against the grain, urging users not to spread #fakenews and to "leave it to professionals," which implies deference rather than distrust [T4-005389](#T4-005389), and T4-003494 addresses individual agency rather than media reliability, sharing nothing relevant [T4-003494](#T4-003494).
